582	def set_signature(
583	    model_uri: str,
584	    signature: ModelSignature,
585	):
586	    """
587	    Sets the model signature for specified model artifacts.
588	
589	    The process involves downloading the MLmodel file in the model artifacts (if it's non-local),
590	    updating its model signature, and then overwriting the existing MLmodel file. Should the
591	    artifact repository associated with the model artifacts disallow overwriting, this function will
592	    fail.
593	
594	    Furthermore, as model registry artifacts are read-only, model artifacts located in the
595	    model registry and represented by ``models:/`` URI schemes are not compatible with this API.
596	    To set a signature on a model version, first load the source model artifacts. Following this,
597	    generate a new model version using the loaded model artifacts and a corresponding signature.
598	    For more information about setting signatures on model versions, see
599	    `this doc section <https://mlflow.org/docs/latest/ml/model/signatures/#adding-signatures-to-registered-model-versions>`_.
600	
601	    Args:
602	        model_uri: The location, in URI format, of the MLflow model. For example:
603	
604	            - ``/Users/me/path/to/local/model``
605	            - ``relative/path/to/local/model``
606	            - ``s3://my_bucket/path/to/model``
607	            - ``runs:/<mlflow_run_id>/run-relative/path/to/model``
608	            - ``mlflow-artifacts:/path/to/model``
609	            - ``models:/<model_id>``
610	
611	            For more information about supported URI schemes, see
612	            `Referencing Artifacts <https://www.mlflow.org/docs/latest/concepts.html#
613	            artifact-locations>`_.
614	
615	            Please note that model URIs with the ``models:/<name>/<version>`` scheme are not
616	            supported.
617	
618	        signature: ModelSignature to set on the model.
619	
620	    .. code-block:: python
621	        :caption: Example
622	
623	        import mlflow
624	        from mlflow.models import set_signature, infer_signature
625	
626	        # load model from run artifacts
627	        run_id = "96771d893a5e46159d9f3b49bf9013e2"
628	        artifact_path = "models"
629	        model_uri = f"runs:/{run_id}/{artifact_path}"
630	        model = mlflow.pyfunc.load_model(model_uri)
631	
632	        # determine model signature
633	        test_df = ...
634	        predictions = model.predict(test_df)

182	def infer_signature(
183	    model_input: Any = None,
184	    model_output: "MlflowInferableDataset" = None,
185	    params: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
186	) -> ModelSignature:
187	    """
188	    Infer an MLflow model signature from the training data (input), model predictions (output)
189	    and parameters (for inference).
190	
191	    The signature represents model input and output as data frames with (optionally) named columns
192	    and data type specified as one of types defined in :py:class:`mlflow.types.DataType`. It also
193	    includes parameters schema for inference, .
194	    This method will raise an exception if the user data contains incompatible types or is not
195	    passed in one of the supported formats listed below.
196	
197	    The input should be one of these:
198	      - pandas.DataFrame
199	      - pandas.Series
200	      - dictionary of { name -> numpy.ndarray}
201	      - numpy.ndarray
202	      - pyspark.sql.DataFrame
203	      - scipy.sparse.csr_matrix
204	      - scipy.sparse.csc_matrix
205	      - dictionary / list of dictionaries of JSON-convertible types
206	
207	    The element types should be mappable to one of :py:class:`mlflow.types.DataType`.
208	
209	    For pyspark.sql.DataFrame inputs, columns of type DateType and TimestampType are both inferred
210	    as type :py:data:`datetime <mlflow.types.DataType.datetime>`, which is coerced to
211	    TimestampType at inference.
212	
213	    Args:
214	      model_input: Valid input to the model. E.g. (a subset of) the training dataset.
215	      model_output: Valid model output. E.g. Model predictions for the (subset of) training
216	                    dataset.
217	      params: Valid parameters for inference. It should be a dictionary of parameters
218	              that can be set on the model during inference by passing `params` to pyfunc
219	              `predict` method.
220	
221	              An example of valid parameters:
222	
223	              .. code-block:: python
224	
225	                    from mlflow.models import infer_signature
226	                    from mlflow.transformers import generate_signature_output
227	
228	                    # Define parameters for inference
229	                    params = {
230	                        "num_beams": 5,
231	                        "max_length": 30,
232	                        "do_sample": True,
233	                        "remove_invalid_values": True,
234	                    }
235	
236	                    # Infer the signature including parameters
237	                    signature = infer_signature(
238	                        data,
239	                        generate_signature_output(model, data),
240	                        params=params,
241	                    )
242	
243	                    # Saving model with model signature
244	                    mlflow.transformers.save_model(
245	                        model,
246	                        path=model_path,
247	                        signature=signature,
248	                    )
249	
250	                    pyfunc_loaded = mlflow.pyfunc.load_model(model_path)
251	
252	                    # Passing params to `predict` function directly
253	                    result = pyfunc_loaded.predict(data, params=params)
254	
255	    Returns:
256	      ModelSignature
257	    """
258	    schemas = {"inputs": model_input, "outputs": model_output}
259	    for key, data in schemas.items():
260	        if data is not None:
261	            try:
262	                schemas[key] = (
263	                    convert_dataclass_to_schema(data) if is_dataclass(data) else _infer_schema(data)
264	                )
265	            except InvalidDataForSignatureInferenceError:
266	                raise
267	            except Exception:
268	                extra_msg = (
269	                    ("Note that MLflow doesn't validate data types during inference for AnyType. ")
270	                    if key == "inputs"
271	                    else ""
272	                )
273	                _logger.warning(
274	                    f"Failed to infer schema for {key}. "
275	                    f"Setting schema to `Schema([ColSpec(type=AnyType())]` as default. {extra_msg}"
276	                    "To see the full traceback, set logging level to DEBUG.",
277	                    exc_info=_logger.isEnabledFor(logging.DEBUG),
278	                )
279	                schemas[key] = Schema([ColSpec(type=AnyType())])
280	    schemas["params"] = _infer_param_schema(params) if params else None
281	    return ModelSignature(**schemas)

323	def _extract_type_hints(f, input_arg_index):
324	    """
325	    Extract type hints from a function.
326	
327	    Args:
328	        f: Function to extract type hints from.
329	        input_arg_index: Index of the function argument that corresponds to the model input.
330	
331	    Returns:
332	        A `_TypeHints` object containing the input and output type hints.
333	    """
334	    if not hasattr(f, "__annotations__") and hasattr(f, "__call__"):
335	        return _extract_type_hints(f.__call__, input_arg_index)
336	
337	    if f.__annotations__ == {}:
338	        return _TypeHints()
339	
340	    arg_names = list(filter(lambda x: x != "self", _get_arg_names(f)))
341	    if len(arg_names) - 1 < input_arg_index:
342	        raise MlflowException.invalid_parameter_value(
343	            f"The specified input argument index ({input_arg_index}) is out of range for the "
344	            "function signature: {}".format(input_arg_index, arg_names)
345	        )
346	    arg_name = arg_names[input_arg_index]
347	    try:
348	        hints = get_type_hints(f)
349	    except (
350	        TypeError,
351	        NameError,  # To handle this issue: https://github.com/python/typing/issues/797
352	    ):
353	        # ---
354	        # from __future__ import annotations # postpones evaluation of 'list[str]'
355	        #
356	        # def f(x: list[str]) -> list[str]:
357	        #          ^^^^^^^^^ Evaluating this expression ('list[str]') results in a TypeError in
358	        #                    Python < 3.9 because the built-in list type is not subscriptable.
359	        #     return x
360	        # ---
361	        # Best effort to infer type hints from strings
362	        hints = {}
363	        for arg in [arg_name, "return"]:
364	            if hint_str := f.__annotations__.get(arg, None):
365	                if hint := _infer_hint_from_str(hint_str):
366	                    hints[arg] = hint
367	                else:
368	                    _logger.info("Unsupported type hint: %s, skipping schema inference", hint_str)
369	    except Exception as e:
370	        _logger.warning("Failed to extract type hints from function %s: %s", f.__name__, repr(e))
371	        return _TypeHints()
372	
373	    return _TypeHints(hints.get(arg_name), hints.get("return"))

376	def _is_context_in_predict_function_signature(*, func=None, parameters=None):
377	    if parameters is None:
378	        if func is None:
379	            raise ValueError("Either `func` or `parameters` must be provided.")
380	        parameters = inspect.signature(func).parameters
381	    return (
382	        # predict(self, context, model_input, ...)
383	        "context" in parameters
384	        # predict(self, ctx, model_input, ...) ctx can be any parameter name
385	        or len([param for param in parameters if param not in ("self", "params")]) == 2
386	    )

390	def _infer_signature_from_type_hints(
391	    python_model, context, type_hints: _TypeHints, input_example=None
392	) -> ModelSignature | None:
393	    """
394	    Infer the signature from type hints.
395	    """
396	    if type_hints.input is None:
397	        return None
398	
399	    params = None
400	    params_key = "params"
401	    if _contains_params(input_example):
402	        input_example, params = input_example
403	
404	    try:
405	        input_schema = _infer_schema_from_list_type_hint(type_hints.input)
406	    except InvalidTypeHintException:
407	        raise MlflowException.invalid_parameter_value(
408	            "The `predict` function has unsupported type hints for the model input "
409	            "arguments. Update it to one of supported type hints, or remove type hints "
410	            "to bypass this check. Error: {e}"
411	        )
412	    except Exception as e:
413	        warnings.warn(f"Failed to infer signature from type hint: {e.message}", stacklevel=3)
414	        return None
415	
416	    func = python_model if callable(python_model) else python_model.predict
417	
418	    # only warn if the pyfunc decorator is not used and schema can
419	    # be inferred from the input type hint
420	    _pyfunc_decorator_used = getattr(func, "_is_pyfunc", False)
421	    if not _pyfunc_decorator_used:
422	        # stacklevel is 3 because we have a decorator
423	        warnings.warn(
424	            "Decorate your function with `@mlflow.pyfunc.utils.pyfunc` to enable auto "
425	            "data validation against model input type hints.",
426	            stacklevel=3,
427	        )
428	
429	    default_output_schema = Schema([ColSpec(type=AnyType())])
430	    is_output_type_hint_valid = False
431	    output_schema = None
432	    if type_hints.output:
433	        try:
434	            # output type hint doesn't need to be a list
435	            # but if it's a list, we infer the schema from the list type hint
436	            # to be consistent with input schema inference
437	            output_schema = (
438	                _infer_schema_from_list_type_hint(type_hints.output)
439	                if _is_list_type_hint(type_hints.output)
440	                else _infer_schema_from_type_hint(type_hints.output)
441	            )
442	            is_output_type_hint_valid = True
443	        except Exception as e:
444	            _logger.info(
445	                f"Failed to infer output type hint, setting output schema to AnyType. {e}",
446	                stacklevel=2,
447	            )
448	            output_schema = default_output_schema
449	    else:
450	        output_schema = default_output_schema
451	    params_schema = _infer_param_schema(params) if params else None
452	
453	    if input_example is not None:
454	        # only validate input example here if pyfunc decorator is not used
455	        # because when the decorator is used, the input is validated in the predict function
456	        if not _pyfunc_decorator_used and (
457	            msg := _get_data_validation_result(
458	                data=input_example, type_hint=type_hints.input
459	            ).error_message
460	        ):
461	            _logger.warning(
462	                "Input example is not compatible with the type hint of the `predict` function. "
463	                f"Error: {msg}"
464	            )
465	        else:
466	            kwargs = (
467	                {params_key: params}
468	                if params and params_key in inspect.signature(func).parameters
469	                else {}
470	            )
471	            # This is for PythonModel's predict function
472	            if _is_context_in_predict_function_signature(func=func):
473	                inputs = [None, input_example]
474	            else:
475	                inputs = [input_example]
476	            _logger.info("Running the predict function to generate output based on input example")
477	            try:
478	                if hasattr(python_model, "load_context"):
479	                    python_model.load_context(context)
480	                output_example = func(*inputs, **kwargs)
481	            except Exception:
482	                _logger.warning(
483	                    "Failed to run the predict function on input example. To see the full "
484	                    "traceback, set logging level to DEBUG.",
485	                    exc_info=_logger.isEnabledFor(logging.DEBUG),
486	                )
487	            else:
488	                if is_output_type_hint_valid and (
489	                    msg := _get_data_validation_result(
490	                        data=output_example, type_hint=type_hints.output
491	                    ).error_message
492	                ):
493	                    _logger.warning(
494	                        f"Failed to validate output `{output_example}` against type hint "
495	                        f"`{type_hints.output}`, setting output schema to AnyType. "
496	                        f"Error: {msg}"
497	                    )
498	                    output_schema = default_output_schema
499	    if not any([input_schema, output_schema, params_schema]):
500	        return None
501	    signature = ModelSignature(inputs=input_schema, outputs=output_schema, params=params_schema)
502	    signature._is_signature_from_type_hint = True
503	    return signature

506	def _infer_signature_from_input_example(
507	    input_example: _Example | None, wrapped_model
508	) -> ModelSignature | None:
509	    """
510	    Infer the signature from an example input and a PyFunc wrapped model. Catches all exceptions.
511	
512	    Args:
513	        input_example: Saved _Example object that contains input example instance.
514	        wrapped_model: A PyFunc wrapped model which has a `predict` method.
515	
516	    Returns:
517	        A `ModelSignature` object containing the inferred schema of both the model's inputs
518	        based on the `input_example` and the model's outputs based on the prediction from the
519	        `wrapped_model`.
520	    """
521	    from mlflow.pyfunc import _validate_prediction_input
522	
523	    if input_example is None:
524	        return None
525	
526	    try:
527	        # Copy the input example so that it is not mutated by predict()
528	        input_data = deepcopy(input_example.inference_data)
529	        params = input_example.inference_params
530	
531	        input_schema = _infer_schema(input_data)
532	        params_schema = _infer_param_schema(params) if params else None
533	        # do the same validation as pyfunc predict to make sure the signature is correctly
534	        # applied to the model
535	        input_data, params = _validate_prediction_input(
536	            input_data, params, input_schema, params_schema
537	        )
538	        prediction = wrapped_model.predict(input_data, params=params)
539	        # For column-based inputs, 1D numpy arrays likely signify row-based predictions. Thus, we
540	        # convert them to a Pandas series for inferring as a single ColSpec Schema.
541	        if (
542	            not input_schema.is_tensor_spec()
543	            and isinstance(prediction, np.ndarray)
544	            and prediction.ndim == 1
545	        ):
546	            prediction = pd.Series(prediction)
547	
548	        output_schema = None
549	        try:
550	            output_schema = _infer_schema(prediction)
551	        except Exception:
552	            # try assign output schema if failing to infer it from prediction for langchain models
553	            try:
554	                from mlflow.langchain.model import _LangChainModelWrapper
555	                from mlflow.langchain.utils.chat import _ChatResponse
556	            except ImportError:
557	                pass
558	            else:
559	                if isinstance(wrapped_model, _LangChainModelWrapper) and isinstance(
560	                    prediction, _ChatResponse
561	                ):
562	                    output_schema = prediction.get_schema()
563	            if output_schema is None:
564	                _logger.warning(
565	                    "Failed to infer model output schema from prediction result, setting "
566	                    "output schema to AnyType. For full traceback, set logging level to debug.",
567	                    exc_info=_logger.isEnabledFor(logging.DEBUG),
568	                )
569	                output_schema = Schema([ColSpec(type=AnyType())])
570	
571	        return ModelSignature(input_schema, output_schema, params_schema)
572	    except Exception as e:
573	        if _MLFLOW_TESTING.get():
574	            raise
575	        _logger.warning(
576	            _LOG_MODEL_INFER_SIGNATURE_WARNING_TEMPLATE,
577	            repr(e),
578	            exc_info=_logger.isEnabledFor(logging.DEBUG),

432	                assert updated_obj == Object(

468	            updated_properties.append(Property(name=k, dtype=prop_dict2[k].dtype, required=False))

1399	def convert_dataclass_to_schema(dataclass):

1401	    Converts a given dataclass into a Schema object. The dataclass must include type hints
1402	    for all its fields. Fields can be of basic types, other dataclasses, or Lists/Optional of
1403	    these types. Union types are not supported. Only the top-level fields are directly converted
1404	    to ColSpecs, while nested fields are converted into nested Object types.
1405	    """
1406	
1407	    inputs = []
1408	
1409	    for field_name, field_type in _get_dataclass_annotations(dataclass).items():
1410	        # Determine the type and handle Optional and List correctly
1411	        is_optional = False
1412	        effective_type = field_type
1413	
1414	        if _is_union(field_type):
1415	            if type(None) in get_args(field_type) and len(get_args(field_type)) == 2:
1416	                # This is an Optional type; determine the effective type excluding None
1417	                is_optional = True
1418	                effective_type = next(t for t in get_args(field_type) if t is not type(None))
1419	            else:
1420	                raise MlflowException(
1421	                    "Only Optional[...] is supported as a Union type in dataclass fields"
1422	                )
1423	
1424	        if get_origin(effective_type) == list:
1425	            # It's a list, check the type within the list
1426	            list_type = get_args(effective_type)[0]
1427	            if is_dataclass(list_type):
1428	                dtype = _convert_dataclass_to_nested_object(list_type)  # Convert to nested Object
1429	                inputs.append(
1430	                    ColSpec(type=Array(dtype=dtype), name=field_name, required=not is_optional)
1431	                )
1432	            else:
1433	                if dtype := _map_field_type(list_type):
1434	                    inputs.append(
1435	                        ColSpec(
1436	                            type=Array(dtype=dtype),
1437	                            name=field_name,
1438	                            required=not is_optional,
1439	                        )
1440	                    )
1441	                else:
1442	                    raise MlflowException(
1443	                        f"List field type {list_type} is not supported in dataclass"
1444	                        f" {dataclass.__name__}"
1445	                    )
1446	        elif is_dataclass(effective_type):
1447	            # It's a nested dataclass
1448	            dtype = _convert_dataclass_to_nested_object(effective_type)  # Convert to nested Object
1449	            inputs.append(
1450	                ColSpec(
1451	                    type=dtype,
1452	                    name=field_name,
1453	                    required=not is_optional,
1454	                )
1455	            )
1456	        # confirm the effective type is a basic type
1457	        elif dtype := _map_field_type(effective_type):
1458	            # It's a basic type
1459	            inputs.append(
1460	                ColSpec(
1461	                    type=dtype,
1462	                    name=field_name,
1463	                    required=not is_optional,
1464	                )
1465	            )
1466	        else:
1467	            raise MlflowException(
1468	                f"Unsupported field type {effective_type} in dataclass {dataclass.__name__}"
1469	            )

1475	    """

1484	def _convert_field_to_property(field_name, field_type):

import base64
import datetime
import json

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import pytest
from google.protobuf.text_format import Parse as ParseTextIntoProto

from mlflow.entities import Experiment, Metric
from mlflow.entities.model_registry import ModelVersion, RegisteredModel
from mlflow.exceptions import MlflowException
from mlflow.protos.model_registry_pb2 import RegisteredModel as ProtoRegisteredModel
from mlflow.protos.service_pb2 import Experiment as ProtoExperiment
from mlflow.protos.service_pb2 import Metric as ProtoMetric
from mlflow.types import ColSpec, DataType, Schema, TensorSpec
from mlflow.types.schema import Array, Map, Object, Property
from mlflow.types.utils import _infer_schema
from mlflow.utils.proto_json_utils import (
    MlflowFailedTypeConversion,
    _CustomJsonEncoder,
    _stringify_all_experiment_ids,
    cast_df_types_according_to_schema,
    dataframe_from_parsed_json,
    dataframe_from_raw_json,
    message_to_json,
    parse_dict,
    parse_tf_serving_input,
)

from tests.protos.test_message_pb2 import SampleMessage


def test_message_to_json():
    json_out = message_to_json(Experiment("123", "name", "arty", "active").to_proto())
    assert json.loads(json_out) == {
        "experiment_id": "123",
        "name": "name",
        "artifact_location": "arty",
        "lifecycle_stage": "active",
    }

    original_proto_message = RegisteredModel(
        name="model_1",
        creation_timestamp=111,
        last_updated_timestamp=222,
        description="Test model",
        latest_versions=[
            ModelVersion(
                name="mv-1",
                version="1",
                creation_timestamp=333,
                last_updated_timestamp=444,
                description="v 1",
                user_id="u1",
                current_stage="Production",
                source="A/B",
                run_id="9245c6ce1e2d475b82af84b0d36b52f4",
                status="READY",
                status_message=None,
            ),
            ModelVersion(
                name="mv-2",
                version="2",
                creation_timestamp=555,
                last_updated_timestamp=666,
                description="v 2",
                user_id="u2",
                current_stage="Staging",
                source="A/C",
                run_id="123",
                status="READY",
                status_message=None,
            ),
        ],
    ).to_proto()
    json_out = message_to_json(original_proto_message)
    json_dict = json.loads(json_out)
    assert json_dict == {
        "name": "model_1",
        "creation_timestamp": 111,
        "last_updated_timestamp": 222,
        "description": "Test model",
        "latest_versions": [
            {
                "name": "mv-1",
                "version": "1",

            {
                "name": "mv-2",
                "version": "2",

577	def parse_instances_data(data, schema=None):
578	    import numpy as np
579	
580	    from mlflow.types.schema import Array

92	            # So we need to replace the str keys with int keys in to_dict.
93	            to_dict[key] = to_dict[str(key)]
94	            del to_dict[str(key)]
95	
96	        if key not in to_dict:
97	            continue
98	
99	        if isinstance(value, dict):
100	            _merge_json_dicts(from_dict[key], to_dict[key])
101	        elif isinstance(value, list):
102	            for i, v in enumerate(value):
103	                if isinstance(v, dict):
104	                    _merge_json_dicts(v, to_dict[key][i])
105	                else:
106	                    to_dict[key][i] = v
107	        else:
108	            to_dict[key] = from_dict[key]
109	    return to_dict

112	def message_to_json(message):
113	    """Converts a message to JSON, using snake_case for field names."""
114	
115	    # Google's MessageToJson API converts int64 proto fields to JSON strings.
116	    # For more info, see https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/2954
117	    json_dict_with_int64_as_str = json.loads(
118	        MessageToJson(message, preserving_proto_field_name=True)
119	    )
120	    # We convert this proto message into a JSON dict where only int64 proto fields
121	    # are preserved, and they are treated as JSON numbers, not strings.
122	    json_dict_with_int64_fields_only = _mark_int64_fields(message)
123	    # By merging these two JSON dicts, we end up with a JSON dict where int64 proto fields are not
124	    # converted to JSON strings. Int64 keys in proto maps will always be converted to JSON strings
125	    # because JSON doesn't support non-string keys.
126	    json_dict_with_int64_as_numbers = _merge_json_dicts(
127	        json_dict_with_int64_fields_only, json_dict_with_int64_as_str
128	    )
129	    return json.dumps(json_dict_with_int64_as_numbers, indent=2)

174	def _stringify_all_experiment_ids(x):
175	    """Converts experiment_id fields which are defined as ints into strings in the given json.
176	    This is necessary for backwards- and forwards-compatibility with MLflow clients/servers
177	    running MLflow 0.9.0 and below, as experiment_id was changed from an int to a string.

179	    server or client that sees the new format is fine), but is unwilling to convert ints
180	    to strings. Therefore, we need to manually perform this conversion.

183	    upgrade clients and servers to MLflow 0.9.1+.

192	            elif k == "info" and isinstance(v, dict) and "experiment_id" in v and "run_uuid" in v:
193	                # shortcut for run info

195	            elif k not in ("params", "tags", "metrics"):  # skip run data
196	                _stringify_all_experiment_ids(v)
197	    elif isinstance(x, list):

243	    elif proto.HasField("list_value"):

255	class NumpyEncoder(JSONEncoder):
256	    """Special json encoder for numpy types.
257	    Note that some numpy types doesn't have native python equivalence,
258	    hence json.dumps will raise TypeError.
259	    In this case, you'll need to convert your numpy types into its closest python equivalence.
260	    """
261	
262	    def try_convert(self, o):
263	        import numpy as np
264	        import pandas as pd
265	
266	        def encode_binary(x):
267	            return base64.encodebytes(x).decode("ascii")
268	
269	        if isinstance(o, np.ndarray):
270	            if o.dtype == object:
271	                return [self.try_convert(x)[0] for x in o.tolist()], True
272	            elif o.dtype == np.bytes_:
273	                return np.vectorize(encode_binary)(o), True
274	            else:
275	                return o.tolist(), True
276	
277	        if isinstance(o, np.generic):
278	            return o.item(), True
279	        if isinstance(o, (bytes, bytearray)):
280	            return encode_binary(o), True
281	        if isinstance(o, np.datetime64):
282	            return np.datetime_as_string(o), True
283	        if isinstance(o, (pd.Timestamp, datetime.date, datetime.datetime, datetime.time)):
284	            return o.isoformat(), True
285	        if isinstance(o, pydantic.BaseModel):
286	            return o.model_dump(), True
287	        return o, False
288	
289	    def default(self, o):
290	        res, converted = self.try_convert(o)
291	        if converted:
292	            return res
293	        else:
294	            return super().default(o)

310	def cast_df_types_according_to_schema(pdf, schema):
311	    import numpy as np
312	
313	    from mlflow.models.utils import _enforce_array, _enforce_map, _enforce_object
314	    from mlflow.types.schema import AnyType, Array, DataType, Map, Object
315	
316	    actual_cols = set(pdf.columns)
317	    if schema.has_input_names():
318	        dtype_list = zip(schema.input_names(), schema.input_types())
319	    elif schema.is_tensor_spec() and len(schema.input_types()) == 1:
320	        dtype_list = zip(actual_cols, [schema.input_types()[0] for _ in actual_cols])
321	    else:
322	        n = min(len(schema.input_types()), len(pdf.columns))
323	        dtype_list = zip(pdf.columns[:n], schema.input_types()[:n])
324	    required_input_names = set(schema.required_input_names())
325	
326	    for col_name, col_type_spec in dtype_list:
327	        if isinstance(col_type_spec, DataType):
328	            col_type = col_type_spec.to_pandas()
329	        else:
330	            col_type = col_type_spec
331	        if col_name in actual_cols:
332	            required = col_name in required_input_names
333	            try:
334	                if isinstance(col_type_spec, DataType) and col_type_spec == DataType.binary:
335	                    # NB: We expect binary data to be passed base64 encoded
336	                    pdf[col_name] = pdf[col_name].map(
337	                        lambda x: base64.decodebytes(bytes(x, "utf8"))
338	                    )
339	                elif col_type == np.dtype(bytes):
340	                    pdf[col_name] = pdf[col_name].map(lambda x: bytes(x, "utf8"))
341	                elif schema.is_tensor_spec() and isinstance(pdf[col_name].iloc[0], list):
342	                    # For dataframe with multidimensional column, it contains
343	                    # list type values, we cannot convert
344	                    # its type by `astype`, skip conversion.
345	                    # The conversion will be done in `_enforce_schema` while
346	                    # `PyFuncModel.predict` being called.
347	                    pass
348	                elif isinstance(col_type_spec, Array):
349	                    pdf[col_name] = pdf[col_name].map(
350	                        lambda x: _enforce_array(x, col_type_spec, required=required)
351	                    )
352	                elif isinstance(col_type_spec, Object):
353	                    pdf[col_name] = pdf[col_name].map(
354	                        lambda x: _enforce_object(x, col_type_spec, required=required)
355	                    )
356	                elif isinstance(col_type_spec, Map):
357	                    pdf[col_name] = pdf[col_name].map(
358	                        lambda x: _enforce_map(x, col_type_spec, required=required)
359	                    )
360	                elif isinstance(col_type_spec, AnyType):
361	                    pass
362	                else:
363	                    pdf[col_name] = pdf[col_name].astype(col_type, copy=False)
364	            except Exception as ex:
365	                raise MlflowFailedTypeConversion(col_name, col_type, ex)
366	    return pdf

369	def dataframe_from_parsed_json(decoded_input, pandas_orient, schema=None):
370	    """Convert parsed json into pandas.DataFrame. If schema is provided this methods will attempt to
371	    cast data types according to the schema. This include base64 decoding for binary columns.
372	
373	    Args:
374	        decoded_input: Parsed json - either a list or a dictionary.
375	        pandas_orient: pandas data frame convention used to store the data.
376	        schema: MLflow schema used when parsing the data.
377	
378	    Returns:
379	        pandas.DataFrame.
380	    """
381	    import pandas as pd
382	
383	    if pandas_orient == "records":
384	        if not isinstance(decoded_input, list):
385	            if isinstance(decoded_input, dict):
386	                typemessage = "dictionary"
387	            else:
388	                typemessage = f"type {type(decoded_input)}"
389	            raise MlflowInvalidInputException(
390	                f"Dataframe records format must be a list of records. Got {typemessage}."
391	            )
392	        try:
393	            pdf = pd.DataFrame(data=decoded_input)
394	        except Exception as ex:
395	            raise MlflowInvalidInputException(
396	                f"Provided dataframe_records field is not a valid dataframe representation in "
397	                f"'records' format. Error: '{ex}'"
398	            )
399	    elif pandas_orient == "split":
400	        if not isinstance(decoded_input, dict):
401	            if isinstance(decoded_input, list):
402	                typemessage = "list"
403	            else:
404	                typemessage = f"type {type(decoded_input)}"
405	            raise MlflowInvalidInputException(
406	                f"Dataframe split format must be a dictionary. Got {typemessage}."
407	            )
408	        keys = set(decoded_input.keys())
409	        missing_data = "data" not in keys
410	        extra_keys = keys.difference({"columns", "data", "index"})
411	        if missing_data or extra_keys:
412	            raise MlflowInvalidInputException(
413	                f"Dataframe split format must have 'data' field and optionally 'columns' "
414	                f"and 'index' fields. Got {keys}.'"
415	            )
416	        try:
417	            pdf = pd.DataFrame(
418	                index=decoded_input.get("index"),
419	                columns=decoded_input.get("columns"),
420	                data=decoded_input["data"],
421	            )
422	        except Exception as ex:
423	            raise MlflowInvalidInputException(
424	                f"Provided dataframe_split field is not a valid dataframe representation in "
425	                f"'split' format. Error: '{ex}'"
426	            )
427	    if schema is not None:
428	        pdf = cast_df_types_according_to_schema(pdf, schema)
429	    return pdf

479	def convert_data_type(data, spec):
480	    """
481	    Convert input data to the type specified in the spec.
482	
483	    Args:
484	        data: Input data.
485	        spec: ColSpec or TensorSpec.
486	    """
487	    import numpy as np
488	
489	    from mlflow.models.utils import _enforce_array, _enforce_map, _enforce_object
490	    from mlflow.types.schema import AnyType, Array, ColSpec, DataType, Map, Object, TensorSpec
491	
492	    try:
493	        if spec is None:
494	            return np.array(data)
495	        if isinstance(spec, TensorSpec):
496	            return np.array(data, dtype=spec.type)
497	        if isinstance(spec, ColSpec):
498	            if isinstance(spec.type, DataType):
499	                return (
500	                    np.array(data, spec.type.to_numpy())
501	                    if isinstance(data, (list, np.ndarray))
502	                    else np.array([data], spec.type.to_numpy())[0]
503	                )
504	            elif isinstance(spec.type, Array):
505	                # convert to numpy array for backwards compatibility
506	                return np.array(_enforce_array(data, spec.type, required=spec.required))
507	            elif isinstance(spec.type, Object):
508	                return _enforce_object(data, spec.type, required=spec.required)
509	            elif isinstance(spec.type, Map):
510	                return _enforce_map(data, spec.type, required=spec.required)
511	            elif isinstance(spec.type, AnyType):
512	                return data
513	    except MlflowException as e:
514	        raise MlflowInvalidInputException(e.message)
515	    except Exception as ex:
516	        raise MlflowInvalidInputException(f"{ex}")
517	
518	    raise MlflowInvalidInputException(
519	        f"Failed to convert data type for data `{data}` with spec `{spec}`."
520	    )

523	def _cast_schema_type(input_data, schema=None):
524	    import numpy as np
525	
526	    input_data = deepcopy(input_data)
527	    # spec_name -> spec mapping
528	    types_dict = schema.input_dict() if schema and schema.has_input_names() else {}
529	    if schema is not None:
530	        if (
531	            len(types_dict) == 1
532	            and isinstance(input_data, list)
533	            and not any(isinstance(x, dict) for x in input_data)
534	        ):
535	            # for data with a single column (not List[Dict]), match input with column
536	            input_data = {next(iter(types_dict)): input_data}
537	        # Un-named schema should only contain a single column or a single value
538	        elif not schema.has_input_names() and not (
539	            isinstance(input_data, list) or np.isscalar(input_data)
540	        ):
541	            raise MlflowInvalidInputException(
542	                "Failed to parse input data. This model contains an un-named "
543	                " model signature which expects a single n-dimensional array or "
544	                "a single value as input, however, an input of type "
545	                f"{type(input_data)} was found."
546	            )
547	    if isinstance(input_data, dict):
548	        # each key corresponds to a column, values should be
549	        # checked against the schema
550	        input_data = {
551	            col: convert_data_type(data, types_dict.get(col)) for col, data in input_data.items()
552	        }
553	    elif isinstance(input_data, list):
554	        # List of dictionaries of column_name -> value mapping
555	        # List[Dict] must correspond to a schema with named columns
556	        if all(isinstance(x, dict) for x in input_data):
557	            input_data = [
558	                {col: convert_data_type(value, types_dict.get(col)) for col, value in data.items()}
559	                for data in input_data
560	            ]
561	        # List of values
562	        else:
563	            spec = schema.inputs[0] if schema else None
564	            input_data = convert_data_type(input_data, spec)
565	    else:
566	        spec = schema.inputs[0] if schema else None
567	        try:
568	            input_data = convert_data_type(input_data, spec)
569	        except Exception as e:
570	            raise MlflowInvalidInputException(
571	                f"Failed to convert data `{input_data}` to type `{spec}` defined "
572	                "in the model signature."
573	            ) from e
574	    return input_data

577	def parse_instances_data(data, schema=None):
578	    import numpy as np
579	
580	    from mlflow.types.schema import Array
581	
582	    if "instances" not in data:
583	        raise MlflowInvalidInputException("Expecting data to have `instances` as key.")
584	    data = data["instances"]
585	    # List[Dict]
586	    if isinstance(data, list) and len(data) > 0 and isinstance(data[0], dict):
587	        # convert items to column format (map column/input name to tensor)
588	        data_dict = defaultdict(list)
589	        types_dict = schema.input_dict() if schema and schema.has_input_names() else {}
590	        for item in data:
591	            for col, v in item.items():
592	                data_dict[col].append(convert_data_type(v, types_dict.get(col)))
593	        # convert to numpy array for backwards compatibility
594	        data = {col: np.array(v) for col, v in data_dict.items()}
595	    else:
596	        data = _cast_schema_type(data, schema)
597	
598	    # Sanity check inputted data. This check will only be applied
599	    # when the row-format `instances` is used since it requires
600	    # same 0-th dimension for all items.
601	    if isinstance(data, dict):
602	        # ensure all columns have the same number of items
603	        # Only check the data when it's a list or numpy array
604	        check_data = {k: v for k, v in data.items() if isinstance(v, (list, np.ndarray))}
605	        if schema and schema.has_input_names():
606	            # Only check required columns
607	            required_cols = schema.required_input_names()
608	            # For Array schema we should not check the length of the data matching
609	            check_cols = {
610	                col for col, spec in schema.input_dict().items() if not isinstance(spec.type, Array)
611	            }
612	            check_cols = list(set(required_cols) & check_cols & set(check_data.keys()))
613	        else:
614	            check_cols = list(check_data.keys())
615	
616	        if check_cols:
617	            expected_len = len(check_data[check_cols[0]])
618	            if not all(len(check_data[col]) == expected_len for col in check_cols[1:]):
619	                raise MlflowInvalidInputException(
620	                    "The length of values for each input/column name are not the same"
621	                )
622	    return data

645	def parse_tf_serving_input(inp_dict, schema=None):
646	    """
647	    Args:
648	        inp_dict: A dict deserialized from a JSON string formatted as described in TF's
649	            serving API doc
650	            (https://www.tensorflow.org/tfx/serving/api_rest#request_format_2)
651	        schema: MLflow schema used when parsing the data.
652	    """

655	        raise MlflowInvalidInputException('"signature_name" parameter is currently not supported')
656	
657	    if not (list(inp_dict.keys()) == ["instances"] or list(inp_dict.keys()) == ["inputs"]):

659	            'One of "instances" and "inputs" must be specified (not both or any other keys).'
660	            f"Received: {list(inp_dict.keys())}"
661	        )

664	    try:
665	        # objects & arrays schema for List[Dict] and Dict[List] are different

33	    """Converts a proto map to JSON, preserving only int64-related fields."""
34	    json_dict = {}
35	    for key, value in proto_map.items():
36	        # The value of a protobuf map can only be a scalar or a message (not a map or repeated
37	        # field).
38	        if value_field_type == FieldDescriptor.TYPE_MESSAGE:
39	            json_dict[key] = _mark_int64_fields(value)
40	        elif value_field_type in _PROTOBUF_INT64_FIELDS:
41	            json_dict[key] = int(value)

47	def _mark_int64_fields(proto_message):
48	    """Converts a proto message to JSON, preserving only int64-related fields."""
49	    json_dict = {}
50	    for field, value in proto_message.ListFields():
51	        if (
52	            # These three conditions check if this field is a protobuf map.
53	            # See the official implementation: https://bit.ly/3EMx1rl
54	            field.type == FieldDescriptor.TYPE_MESSAGE
55	            and field.message_type.has_options
56	            and field.message_type.GetOptions().map_entry
57	        ):
58	            # Deal with proto map fields separately in another function.
59	            json_dict[field.name] = _mark_int64_fields_for_proto_maps(
60	                value, field.message_type.fields_by_name["value"].type
61	            )
62	            continue
63	
64	        if field.type == FieldDescriptor.TYPE_MESSAGE:
65	            ftype = partial(_mark_int64_fields)
66	        elif field.type in _PROTOBUF_INT64_FIELDS:
67	            ftype = int
68	        else:
69	            # Skip all non-int64 fields.
70	            continue
71	
72	        # Use is_repeated property (preferred) with fallback to deprecated label
73	        try:
74	            is_repeated = field.is_repeated
75	        except AttributeError:
76	            is_repeated = field.label == FieldDescriptor.LABEL_REPEATED
77	
78	        json_dict[field.name] = [ftype(v) for v in value] if is_repeated else ftype(value)
79	    return json_dict

82	def _merge_json_dicts(from_dict, to_dict):
83	    """Merges the json elements of from_dict into to_dict. Only works for json dicts
84	    converted from proto messages
85	    """
86	    for key, value in from_dict.items():
87	        if isinstance(key, int) and str(key) in to_dict:
88	            # When the key (i.e. the proto field name) is an integer, it must be a proto map field
89	            # with integer as the key. For example:
90	            # from_dict is {'field_map': {1: '2', 3: '4'}}
91	            # to_dict is {'field_map': {'1': '2', '3': '4'}}
92	            # So we need to replace the str keys with int keys in to_dict.
93	            to_dict[key] = to_dict[str(key)]
94	            del to_dict[str(key)]
95	
96	        if key not in to_dict:
97	            continue
98	
99	        if isinstance(value, dict):
100	            _merge_json_dicts(from_dict[key], to_dict[key])
101	        elif isinstance(value, list):
102	            for i, v in enumerate(value):
103	                if isinstance(v, dict):
104	                    _merge_json_dicts(v, to_dict[key][i])
105	                else:
106	                    to_dict[key][i] = v
107	        else:
108	            to_dict[key] = from_dict[key]
109	    return to_dict

112	def message_to_json(message):
113	    """Converts a message to JSON, using snake_case for field names."""
114	
115	    # Google's MessageToJson API converts int64 proto fields to JSON strings.
116	    # For more info, see https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/2954

118	        MessageToJson(message, preserving_proto_field_name=True)

124	    # converted to JSON strings. Int64 keys in proto maps will always be converted to JSON strings

127	        json_dict_with_int64_fields_only, json_dict_with_int64_as_str
128	    )

255	class NumpyEncoder(JSONEncoder):
256	    """Special json encoder for numpy types.
257	    Note that some numpy types doesn't have native python equivalence,
258	    hence json.dumps will raise TypeError.
259	    In this case, you'll need to convert your numpy types into its closest python equivalence.
260	    """
261	
262	    def try_convert(self, o):
263	        import numpy as np
264	        import pandas as pd
265	
266	        def encode_binary(x):
267	            return base64.encodebytes(x).decode("ascii")
268	
269	        if isinstance(o, np.ndarray):
270	            if o.dtype == object:
271	                return [self.try_convert(x)[0] for x in o.tolist()], True
272	            elif o.dtype == np.bytes_:
273	                return np.vectorize(encode_binary)(o), True
274	            else:
275	                return o.tolist(), True
276	
277	        if isinstance(o, np.generic):
278	            return o.item(), True
279	        if isinstance(o, (bytes, bytearray)):
280	            return encode_binary(o), True
281	        if isinstance(o, np.datetime64):
282	            return np.datetime_as_string(o), True
283	        if isinstance(o, (pd.Timestamp, datetime.date, datetime.datetime, datetime.time)):
284	            return o.isoformat(), True
285	        if isinstance(o, pydantic.BaseModel):
286	            return o.model_dump(), True
287	        return o, False
288	
289	    def default(self, o):
290	        res, converted = self.try_convert(o)
291	        if converted:
292	            return res
293	        else:
294	            return super().default(o)

310	def cast_df_types_according_to_schema(pdf, schema):
311	    import numpy as np
312	
313	    from mlflow.models.utils import _enforce_array, _enforce_map, _enforce_object
314	    from mlflow.types.schema import AnyType, Array, DataType, Map, Object
315	
316	    actual_cols = set(pdf.columns)
317	    if schema.has_input_names():
318	        dtype_list = zip(schema.input_names(), schema.input_types())
319	    elif schema.is_tensor_spec() and len(schema.input_types()) == 1:
320	        dtype_list = zip(actual_cols, [schema.input_types()[0] for _ in actual_cols])
321	    else:
322	        n = min(len(schema.input_types()), len(pdf.columns))
323	        dtype_list = zip(pdf.columns[:n], schema.input_types()[:n])
324	    required_input_names = set(schema.required_input_names())
325	
326	    for col_name, col_type_spec in dtype_list:
327	        if isinstance(col_type_spec, DataType):
328	            col_type = col_type_spec.to_pandas()
329	        else:
330	            col_type = col_type_spec
331	        if col_name in actual_cols:
332	            required = col_name in required_input_names
333	            try:
334	                if isinstance(col_type_spec, DataType) and col_type_spec == DataType.binary:
335	                    # NB: We expect binary data to be passed base64 encoded
336	                    pdf[col_name] = pdf[col_name].map(
337	                        lambda x: base64.decodebytes(bytes(x, "utf8"))
338	                    )
339	                elif col_type == np.dtype(bytes):
340	                    pdf[col_name] = pdf[col_name].map(lambda x: bytes(x, "utf8"))
341	                elif schema.is_tensor_spec() and isinstance(pdf[col_name].iloc[0], list):
342	                    # For dataframe with multidimensional column, it contains
343	                    # list type values, we cannot convert
344	                    # its type by `astype`, skip conversion.
345	                    # The conversion will be done in `_enforce_schema` while
346	                    # `PyFuncModel.predict` being called.
347	                    pass
348	                elif isinstance(col_type_spec, Array):
349	                    pdf[col_name] = pdf[col_name].map(
350	                        lambda x: _enforce_array(x, col_type_spec, required=required)
351	                    )
352	                elif isinstance(col_type_spec, Object):
353	                    pdf[col_name] = pdf[col_name].map(
354	                        lambda x: _enforce_object(x, col_type_spec, required=required)
355	                    )
356	                elif isinstance(col_type_spec, Map):
357	                    pdf[col_name] = pdf[col_name].map(
358	                        lambda x: _enforce_map(x, col_type_spec, required=required)
359	                    )
360	                elif isinstance(col_type_spec, AnyType):
361	                    pass
362	                else:
363	                    pdf[col_name] = pdf[col_name].astype(col_type, copy=False)
364	            except Exception as ex:
365	                raise MlflowFailedTypeConversion(col_name, col_type, ex)
366	    return pdf

369	def dataframe_from_parsed_json(decoded_input, pandas_orient, schema=None):
370	    """Convert parsed json into pandas.DataFrame. If schema is provided this methods will attempt to
371	    cast data types according to the schema. This include base64 decoding for binary columns.
372	
373	    Args:
374	        decoded_input: Parsed json - either a list or a dictionary.
375	        pandas_orient: pandas data frame convention used to store the data.
376	        schema: MLflow schema used when parsing the data.
377	
378	    Returns:
379	        pandas.DataFrame.
380	    """
381	    import pandas as pd
382	
383	    if pandas_orient == "records":
384	        if not isinstance(decoded_input, list):
385	            if isinstance(decoded_input, dict):
386	                typemessage = "dictionary"
387	            else:
388	                typemessage = f"type {type(decoded_input)}"
389	            raise MlflowInvalidInputException(
390	                f"Dataframe records format must be a list of records. Got {typemessage}."
391	            )
392	        try:
393	            pdf = pd.DataFrame(data=decoded_input)
394	        except Exception as ex:
395	            raise MlflowInvalidInputException(
396	                f"Provided dataframe_records field is not a valid dataframe representation in "
397	                f"'records' format. Error: '{ex}'"
398	            )
399	    elif pandas_orient == "split":
400	        if not isinstance(decoded_input, dict):
401	            if isinstance(decoded_input, list):
402	                typemessage = "list"
403	            else:
404	                typemessage = f"type {type(decoded_input)}"
405	            raise MlflowInvalidInputException(
406	                f"Dataframe split format must be a dictionary. Got {typemessage}."
407	            )
408	        keys = set(decoded_input.keys())
409	        missing_data = "data" not in keys
410	        extra_keys = keys.difference({"columns", "data", "index"})
411	        if missing_data or extra_keys:
412	            raise MlflowInvalidInputException(
413	                f"Dataframe split format must have 'data' field and optionally 'columns' "
414	                f"and 'index' fields. Got {keys}.'"
415	            )
416	        try:
417	            pdf = pd.DataFrame(
418	                index=decoded_input.get("index"),
419	                columns=decoded_input.get("columns"),
420	                data=decoded_input["data"],
421	            )
422	        except Exception as ex:
423	            raise MlflowInvalidInputException(
424	                f"Provided dataframe_split field is not a valid dataframe representation in "
425	                f"'split' format. Error: '{ex}'"
426	            )
427	    if schema is not None:
428	        pdf = cast_df_types_according_to_schema(pdf, schema)
429	    return pdf

480	    """
481	    Convert input data to the type specified in the spec.
482	
483	    Args:
484	        data: Input data.
485	        spec: ColSpec or TensorSpec.
486	    """
487	    import numpy as np
488	
489	    from mlflow.models.utils import _enforce_array, _enforce_map, _enforce_object
490	    from mlflow.types.schema import AnyType, Array, ColSpec, DataType, Map, Object, TensorSpec
491	
492	    try:
493	        if spec is None:
494	            return np.array(data)
495	        if isinstance(spec, TensorSpec):
496	            return np.array(data, dtype=spec.type)
497	        if isinstance(spec, ColSpec):
498	            if isinstance(spec.type, DataType):
499	                return (

507	            elif isinstance(spec.type, Object):
